courses.title: Intermediate German I
courses.description: [GE 3B] Review of grammar; conversation; readings in original German.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent, FL 112, GER 1112 , or equivalent.

courses.title: Intermediate German Composition and Conversation
courses.description: Understanding full length motion pictures and other texts in German; speaking at the low intermediate level. Some writing assignments.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent, FL 112, GER 1112 , or equivalent.

courses.title: Intermediate German Reading and Film
courses.description: Development of reading proficiency and of understanding full length motion pictures in German; analysis and discussion of the printed and movie texts. Some translation.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent, FL 211, FL 212, FL 213, GER 2111 , or GER 2113 or equivalent.

courses.title: Special Topics for Lower Division Students
courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: German Civilization
courses.description: Survey of German culture and social customs. Conducted in German.
courses.prerequisites: FL 211, FL 212, FL 213, GER 2111 , or GER 2113 or equivalent.

courses.title: Special Topics for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: World Art: Renaissance through Modern Europe and the United States
courses.description: [GE 3A] Comprehensive survey and analysis of the development of art in Western civilization from the Renaissance through the modern period in Europe and the United States (ca. 15th through 20th centuries).

courses.title: Europe: People, Environment, and Sustainability
courses.description: Analysis and presentations of issues in the natural environment and the cultural landscape of Europe. Major current trends in social, cultural, economic, and political developments in Western and Eastern Europe; relationship between historical and geographical regional diversity.

courses.title: European Revolutions, 1789-1914
courses.description: [GE 4C] Political, social, cultural history of Europe and the European world from the French Revolution until the First World War. Key themes include impact of French and Industrial Revolutions, and emergence of modern nationalism, imperialism, socialism, feminism, and anti-Semitism.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Europe in Crisis, 1900-1945
courses.description: Political, social, cultural, and economic history of Europe from the outbreak of the First World War to the end of the Second World War. Themes include the experiences of combat and the home front in both wars; gender and class anxieties in the aftermath of war and Revolution; the rise and fall of radical authoritarian movements such as Fascism and Nazism.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area A, and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Postwar Europe, 1945-present
courses.description: Political, social, cultural, and economic history of Europe from the end of World War II to the present. Themes include creation and collapse of the Cold War order, emergence of mass consumer society, decolonization and immigration, and future of Europe as united geopolitical identity.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area A, and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: European Governments and Politics
courses.description: Examines the political, economic, and social-cultural institutions and processes of European states and regional organizations. A comparative study of major states in the region is provided, alongside analysis of regional and contemporary challenges.
